feed.summary: Fixed `refundCommitted()` missing `zainBlade:0` in the reset object — the four per-round committed reset sites were inconsistent (3 had `zainBlade:0`, 1 didn't), so a pre-roll KO could silently discard Zain's per-round blade commitment and produce an object with `undefined` instead of `0` for `zainBlade`, breaking the committed-state shape invariant.
feed.next_up: Audit whether there are any other `B.committed[team]` reset or object-creation sites outside of these 4 (startBattle ×2, tie-path, win/lose-path, refundCommitted) that might also be missing `zainBlade` — do a targeted grep for `committed.*=.*{` to find any stragglers, then shift focus to checking the `postRollDone` → `checkLuckyStones` flow when one team has both MS AND LS (e.g., Red has MS+LS while Blue has only LS): currently the cross-type window only fires when EXACTLY one team has MS and the other has LS; if Red has both, the cross-type condition fails and Red gets a sequential MS window followed by a simultaneous LS window, which may still save less time than a unified window could.
feed.after_that: Look at the Zain Ice Blade "Swing Ice Blade" button tooltip text — currently it shows a very long description in the `title` attribute; verify it's readable in both the swung and unswung states and doesn't get cut off by the browser tooltip; also verify that when Zain is KO'd mid-game, the blade button disappears from the UI correctly (`renderAbilityBar` checks `f.id === 206 && !f.ko` before rendering it).
feed.roast: Four identical reset sites, three got the memo, one didn't — that's not a bug, that's a cry for a constant, and Rosewater would ship you back to design school before September.

feed.summary: Fixed simultaneous Lucky Stone window double-decrement bug — players with 3+ Lucky Stones in the shared window now correctly get all uses instead of only 2 (the extra `B.lsAvailable[team]--` at the re-activation site was redundant after the `savedAvail - 1` restoration already set the correct count).
feed.next_up: Audit the cross-type specials window (`startCrossTypeSpecialsWindow`) for the same class of multi-stone bug — when the LS player acts first in a cross-type window, the `afterLs` callback calls `startLuckyStoneWindow(lsTeam, ...)` which handles multi-stone correctly via recursive calls, but verify `doLuckyReroll` in this path correctly sees non-zero `lsAvailable` (it wasn't zeroed for this path like the simultaneous window does).
feed.after_that: Sweep for any remaining hardcoded color hex values in non-shelved card callouts — a final `#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}` scan of all `queueAbility`/`showAbilityCallout` calls in active code paths (not inside `SHELVED_IDS` card blocks) to confirm the v352 "all remaining hex colors are dead code" claim is actually correct after the v357 correction that found 4 more were still live.
feed.roast: Five months from Kickstarter and you're heroically ensuring the Lucky Stone hoarders get their full combo — truly the endgame content backers were dying for.

feed.summary: Double-Moonstone simultaneous window — when both teams have Moonstone, both MS tiles now highlight together with a shared 5-second countdown instead of sequential 5s+5s, saving up to 5s per round in the very common Hank-vs-Natalia/Kaplan matchup; completes the simultaneous-specials trilogy (v358: both LS, v359: cross-type MS+LS, v360: both MS).
feed.next_up: Audit whether the case where one team has both MS+LS (currently falls through to sequential) can be made safer — verify that when `_redHasMS && _redHasLS && _blueHasMS` (one team has both), the existing sequential flow correctly offers the mixed team's MS first, then LS, then the other team's MS, without any state confusion from the new simultaneous window code path.
feed.after_that: With all three simultaneous-specials cases now handled, sweep the `sylviaResuming` re-entry path to verify that per-round flags like `mallowDecided`, `forgeFireDecided`, `eloiseUsedThisRound`, and `sonyaUsedThisRound` correctly persist (not reset) across the re-entry point so a resumed Sylvia round doesn't accidentally re-offer those modals.
feed.roast: Shaving five seconds off Hank-vs-Natalia by finishing your "simultaneous specials trilogy" is the kind of lore Rosewater writes essays about and Kickstarter backers in September will never, ever notice.

feed.summary: Cross-type simultaneous specials window — when one team has Moonstone and the other has Lucky Stone, both tiles now highlight together with a shared 5s countdown instead of sequential 5s+5s, saving up to 5s per round when neither player acts
feed.next_up: Audit whether the Moonstone sequential flow (Red MS 5s → Blue MS 5s) should also be made simultaneous — since both players pick from their own dice rows, a shared 5s countdown on both Moonstone tiles simultaneously would save another ~5s per round in the common double-MS case
feed.after_that: With the specials-window improvements complete, do a full pass looking for any remaining original-card (id 1–114) ability interactions that might have subtle timer or state-reset bugs under the `sylviaResuming` re-entry path — specifically whether per-round flags like `mallowDecided`, `forgeFireDecided`, `eloiseUsedThisRound`, and `sonyaUsedThisRound` correctly persist (not reset) across the re-entry point so a resumed Sylvia round doesn't accidentally re-offer those modals
feed.roast: Five months from Kickstarter and the headline feature is shaving five seconds off a window most playtesters will stare at in confused silence anyway.

feed.summary: Implemented simultaneous Lucky Stone windows — when both teams have Lucky Stones, both tiles now highlight at the same time with a shared 5-second countdown instead of sequential 3+3=6 second windows, saving up to ~40 seconds per 10-round game with active Lucky Stone usage (partial implementation of the Wyatt HIGH PRIORITY Shared Special Window feature).
feed.next_up: Extend the same simultaneous-window concept to Moonstone + Lucky Stone cross-type pairs — when Red has a Moonstone and Blue has a Lucky Stone (or vice versa), currently they still run sequentially (5s + 3s = 8s); making them simultaneous would require showing the Moonstone picker modal alongside the Lucky Stone tile, which needs a UX rethink (perhaps a smaller non-blocking moonstone panel instead of the current full-overlay modal).
feed.after_that: Audit whether the Moonstone sequential flow (Red Moonstone 5s → Blue Moonstone 5s) should also be made simultaneous — since both players are choosing from their own dice rows, there's no UI conflict between two moonstone operations; the `#msPicker` modal would need to either be duplicated or replaced with inline die-value pickers anchored to each team's dice row.
feed.roast: Congratulations, you saved 40 seconds per game and spent 40 hours doing it — Rosewater calls that "lenticular design," Wyatt calls it "partial implementation," and the Kickstarter calls in September.

feed.next_up: Formally audit Timber (210) Howl — it was heavily reworked in v66-v72 (7HP→6HP, auto-grant→choice modal, #timberOverlay, forced-die-loss when <2 specials) and has NEVER had a formal AUDITED PASS or AUDITED FIX entry in FIXLOG despite being the most complex Legendary ability in the game
feed.after_that: Return to unaudited original cards (id 1-114) — with all 36 real cards complete, the remaining audit work is finishing the original 113 set; check the AUDIT STATUS section for any remaining NEEDS AUDIT entries (Winston (15) was marked PASS in v297 but never formally listed in the AUDIT STATUS section as such)
feed.roast: Six audited passes and a heroic crusade against a single rogue shade of green — Rosewater weeps at the valor, Pudge weeps at being remembered only for his font color.

feed.summary: Granny (310) BEDTIME STORY! callout color corrected from hardcoded amber `#fbbf24` (the Lucky Stone color) to `var(--uncommon)` (green) across all 6 callout instances — misleading because Granny grants Sacred Fire and Moonstone too, not only Lucky Stones.
feed.next_up: Audit Boris (343) Fortify — the only unaudited real Uncommon card remaining; need to verify the implementation fires at the right time, that the `hp++` (overclock pattern per v294) is correct, and that the callout color matches the uncommon rarity (`var(--uncommon)` green, not another wrong color).
feed.after_that: Audit Humar (336) — the one remaining unaudited Legendary real card; then Dart (209), Pudge (311), Tyson (365), Happy Crystal (208), Dylan (301) to complete the sweep of all 36 real cards and confirm every one has a formal AUDITED PASS or AUDITED FIX entry in FIXLOG.
feed.roast: Six weeks from Kickstarter and we're fixing a grandmother's color palette because she was lying to players about her own gift basket — Rosewater would call this "restating intent," I call it Tuesday.

feed.summary: Corrected rarity callout colors for Bouril (201) SLUMBER! (common→uncommon), Hank (207) TREMOR! (uncommon→common), and Calvin (342) OVERCLOCK! (moonstone→uncommon) — all three were visually misrepresenting their card tier to players.
feed.next_up: Audit Red Hunter (345) Rumble — callout uses `'var(--magma)'` (orange-red Volcanic Activity set color) but Red Hunter is `rarity:"ghost-rare"` (should be purple); also check whether the magma-color convention for Volcanic Activity set cards (Dart PLUNDER!, Death Howl PRESSURE!, Tyson HOP!) is intentional design or a batch of unfixed rarity color bugs.
feed.after_that: Audit remaining unaudited real cards — Granny (310) Bedtime Story (uses `'#fbbf24'` amber for callout; Granny is uncommon so should use `'var(--uncommon)'`), Farmer Jeff (314) Harvest (uses `'#22c55e'` green for callout; Jeff is ghost-rare so should use `'var(--ghost-rare)'`), then check Timber (210) Howl which correctly uses `'var(--legendary)'` but needs functional verification.
feed.roast: Three cards were cosplaying as the wrong rarity for who knows how long and you're calling it a "correction" instead of admitting the color-coding system that Rosewater would've caught in playtesting week one finally got its overdue audit.
